title: Pork Giniling with Potatoes
blurb: Tomato-braised ground pork with tender potato and carrot cubes.

steps.text: Dice the potato and carrot into 1 cm cubes. Chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the oil in a small pan over medium heat. Soften the onion and garlic, then crumble the pork into the pan and cook until the largest clumps reach 71°C.
Stir in the vegetables, tomato sauce, fish sauce and water. Cover and simmer until the potato is fork-tender, stirring occasionally. Serve over hot rice.

title: Dorm Pinakbet
blurb: Squash, eggplant, long beans and okra simmered in a savory shrimp paste broth.

steps.text: Cut the squash into 2 cm pieces, halve and slice the eggplant, and trim the okra and long beans. Chop the tomato, onion and garlic.
Heat oil and soften the onion, garlic and tomato. Stir in the shrimp paste and water, then bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer the squash for 6 minutes. Add the eggplant, beans and okra and cook until the squash is fork-tender and the beans are just tender. Serve with rice.

title: Ginataang Langka with Tinapa
blurb: Young jackfruit cooked in coconut milk with smoky fish flakes.

steps.text: Slice the peeled young jackfruit thinly. Slice the ginger, garlic and onion, split the chili, and flake the cooked smoked fish, checking carefully for bones.
Combine the coconut milk, water, ginger, garlic and onion in a small pot. Bring to a gentle simmer, then simmer the jackfruit until the thickest pieces are easily pierced with a fork.
Stir in the fish, chili and fish sauce. Return to a simmer and cook until the fish is piping hot throughout. Serve with rice.

title: Chicken Afritada
blurb: Chicken, potatoes and peppers in a lightly sweet tomato stew.

Heat oil over medium heat. Soften the onion and garlic and sear the chicken, turning to color all sides.

Add potato, carrot, tomato sauce, water and salt. Cover and simmer, adding the pepper for the last 4 minutes. Serve with rice once the potato is tender and the center of the largest chicken piece reaches 74°C.

title: Ginisang Upo with Shrimp

Uncover and fold in the shrimp. Simmer gently until the upo is tender and the shrimp flesh is pearly and opaque through the center. Serve with rice.

title: Paksiw na Tilapia

Cover and simmer gently without moving the fish until it reaches 63°C or the center flakes easily and is opaque. Spoon the broth over rice, watching for fish bones.

title: Pritong Galunggong with Tomato Salad

Drain the fish briefly on paper and serve with the tomato salad and rice. Watch for bones.
